title: Times in your own time zone
summary: Every time Intelligence shows, on run timelines, schedules, plans, host monitoring, proposals, email and account pages, now reads in your browser's own time zone and format. Hover a time to see the full date, time and zone. Relative times such as 5m ago are unchanged.
mediaAlt: A workflow run page whose step and What happened timelines show times such as Nov 11, 6:34 PM in the browser's time zone

title: See when workflow requests get answered
summary: Workflows and each run show minutes to the first checked answer, with unchecked sends listed separately. Email and voice requests without checked answers are flagged when they finish; overdue requests are also readable in SQL. Task runs can record answers without owing a reply. Agents use the workflow answer command.
mediaAlt: A completed example email workflow with its step marked done, an unchecked send at 6 minutes and a checked answer at 15 minutes, plus the sent message identifiers

title: Start a queued retry now
summary: When a run's start retry is waiting in its host's queue for capacity, its run page has a Start retry now button. It sends the retry at once, ahead of the queue, and What happened records it. It still counts as one of the three retries, and if it fails it is handled like any other failed retry.
mediaAlt: A run page showing Retry 1 of 3 queued with a Start retry now button; after the click it shows Retry 1 of 3 sent and the timeline says the retry was started by hand, ahead of the queue

title: Let urgent workflows skip the queue
summary: Choose Priority in the workflow editor’s Trigger panel: Automatic follows the trigger, Immediate skips capacity checks, and Normal waits. Automatic email requests and voice memos start immediately, even after changing a task workflow’s trigger. Use Start now on a queued run for a one-time bypass.
mediaAlt: Workflow editor Trigger panel showing Automatic priority after changing a task workflow to a voice memo trigger

title: Page through and search workflow runs
summary: Workflows now lists every run, 50 a page, with Newer and Older links under the table, so older runs are no longer cut off. The search box beside Runs finds runs across all history by any words in their summary, prompt, workflow, status, host, project or branch.
mediaAlt: The Runs list on Workflows: a search for a word narrows it to the matching runs, then Clear and Older page back through history

title: Disk I/O, free space and load in Host monitoring
summary: Host monitoring now charts each host's load against its CPU count, how busy its disks are and how fast they read and write, and lists every local filesystem with its used, free and total space. Hosts on the home page show their load and free disk, and a disk busy more than half the time.
mediaAlt: Host monitoring for a demo host: load, disk busy and disk throughput charts, and a filesystems table with used, free and total space

title: Recover stalled workflow runs
summary: Workflows now nudges an idle orchestrator with its current step when no worker or reply is pending. After two unsuccessful continuations, the run shows Stalled with a reason. Open Workflows or the run page and choose Resume to continue on the same orchestrator and step. Admission queues, startup retries and permission prompts keep their existing rules.
mediaAlt: A sample workflow run marked Stalled, with its recovery reason and Resume button on the run page

title: Queue runs by repository memory needs
summary: The host queue estimates RAM from successful runs of the selected repository, with headroom and a default for repositories without history. The run page shows the estimate. Active runs keep unused memory reserved, and startup retries use the same estimate and FIFO queue.
mediaAlt: A queued application build showing its 10 GiB repository memory estimate and the host memory capacity reason

title: Choose worker models with reusable groups
summary: Create model groups on Plans or Workflows, then insert their tokens into step instructions. Each suggestion balances reachable plan logins using current quota usage, with a model and thinking level you choose. Tokens stay stable when groups are renamed; shared edits affect future suggestions.
mediaAlt: Model groups on Plans, with Frontier and Google frontier tokens, current suggestions, plan labels, and Copy and Edit controls

title: Review proposed workflow runs before they start
summary: MCP clients and host agents can now propose workflow runs. Open Proposals to review the full task and saved workflow, then approve or reject. Nothing starts before approval. Approved proposals link to the resulting run; changed workflows require a fresh proposal.
mediaAlt: A pending workflow run proposal showing its summary, Approve run and Reject controls, full quoted task input and saved workflow

title: Start workflows from voice memos
summary: Choose a PDW voice memo trigger in the workflow editor. Matching recordings start runs with a 1000-character transcript preview and a command to fetch the full transcript. Workflows → Voice memos shows polling status, decisions and links to the matched workflow and run.
mediaAlt: Voice memo history with polling status and a recording linked to its workflow and run

title: Review workflow changes and ask questions
summary: Open Proposals to review a Markdown summary, highlighted changes, and approval controls. Ask a question and an agent answers in the same thread, using desk for context when available. Replies appear automatically, with status and retry controls if an answer cannot start or does not arrive.
mediaAlt: A workflow proposal with its summary and highlighted added instruction, followed by a question and an agent's answer in the discussion thread

title: What's New
summary: A What's New tab now lists each feature as it ships, newest first, with a short summary and a demo. When there are some you have not seen, the tab shows how many and a note appears under the top bar; opening the tab or dismissing the note marks them seen.
mediaAlt: The What's New tab showing 7 unseen features; opening it shows them, newest first, and the count goes away

title: Read Intelligence from MCP clients
summary: Intelligence is now a read-only MCP server at /mcp. Make a token under Account → MCP connections, add it to an MCP client, and that client can query your hosts, agents and workflow runs with SQL. It can read but never change anything.
mediaAlt: Account → MCP connections: Create MCP token shows the MCP URL and a new token (blurred here) once, and lists it as active

title: Attach images to tasks and messages
summary: Add screenshots and other images to a workflow task, a new agent or workspace, or a message in an agent's chat: pick, paste or drop them. The agent gets each image as a file in its worktree.
mediaAlt: Typing a task on Workflows, then attaching two screenshots, which appear as removable thumbnails under the prompt

title: See how long each workflow step took
summary: A workflow run's page now shows how long it spent on each step, and how many times it came back to one, with the current step counting up.
mediaAlt: A workflow run's steps: done steps show their time and how many times the run was on them, and the running step counts up

title: Unattended agents get past permission prompts
summary: When an unattended workflow agent stops on a permission prompt, Intelligence now answers it with an audited denial so the agent carries on, and shows any prompt it could not clear.
mediaAlt: An agent page marked “permission recovery stuck” next to its running and needs-attention badges

title: Start workflows from email
summary: Connect a Gmail mailbox under Workflows → Email, and an email that matches a workflow's senders and filters starts a run of it. Replies in the thread go to that run.
mediaAlt: Workflows → Email: the connected mailbox and what came in, one email ignored as bulk mail and one that started a run; its link opens the run with the email thread

title: Dictate instead of typing
summary: Press ⌘D (or Ctrl+D, or the mic button) in the chat box, a task box or a new agent prompt to speak instead of type. Press it again in an empty box to send.
mediaAlt: Clicking the mic in the task box: the words appear as they are said, then Edit stops and leaves them in the box
